deep.reconstruction:
Context (E477, §§34–36). Euler studies the 'singular series' of order λ = m+n. The meaning below is reconstructed from the formulas and checked numerically against known values. q^μ stands for S(μ, λ−μ) = Σ_x x^{−μ} Σ_{y≤x} y^{−(λ−μ)}, the diagonal y=x included (in modern terms ζ(μ, λ−μ) + ζ(λ)). p^k stands for ζ(k). A column headed p^k (k odd) means the product ζ(k)ζ(λ−k). The p^1 entries are the divergent ζ(1)ζ(λ−1); they cancel in the convergent rows.

On the previous page Euler wrote the order-15 table using even products p^2, p^4, … and called the law 'inductive'. Here (§35) he notes that for odd λ each product ζ(2j)ζ(λ−2j) equals an odd one ζ(λ−2j)ζ(2j). For order 11, p^2 ↔ p^9 and p^4 ↔ p^7. Rewriting with odd columns p^1, p^3, …, p^9 gives a much simpler law.

(1) Coefficient of p^λ = ζ(λ) in q^{λ−ν}: ½(1 + (−1)^{ν+1} C(λ,ν)). For λ=11 these are ½(1+11), ½(1−55), ½(1+165), …

(2) Column p^k: the binomial coefficients C(k−1, j), with alternating signs, are written downward from the top row q^{λ−1} and also upward from the bottom row q^1. Where the two strings overlap, the entries are added.

(3) Rows q^{λ−ν} with ν odd carry the extra term +p^ν p^{λ−ν}.

§36 introduces the notation n(ν) = C(n,ν) in order to state the general odd-weight law on the next page. In modern form this is Euler's theorem: for odd weight, every double zeta value ζ(a,b) is a rational combination of ζ(λ) and the products ζ(k)ζ(λ−k).

Verification.
- Row q^10: S(10,1) = Σ H_n/n^{10} = 6ζ(11) − [ζ(3)ζ(8) + ζ(5)ζ(6) + ζ(7)ζ(4) + ζ(9)ζ(2)]. This agrees with the classical formula Σ H_n/n^q = (1+q/2)ζ(q+1) − ½ Σ_{k=1}^{q−2} ζ(k+1)ζ(q−k).
- Pairs of rows: q^ν + q^{λ−ν} gives ζ(λ) + ζ(ν)ζ(λ−ν) in every pair, i.e. the stuffle relation S(a,b) + S(b,a) = ζ(a)ζ(b) + ζ(λ).
- Columns: every entry of the p^3, p^5, p^7 and p^9 columns matches the top-down/bottom-up binomial rule.
- The same rule for λ=5 gives Σ H_n/n^4 = 3ζ(5) − ζ(2)ζ(3) and Σ H_n^{(2)}/n^3 = 3ζ(2)ζ(3) − (9/2)ζ(5), both correct.
errors: No mathematical errors found: all ten rows of the order-11 table check against the binomial rule and against the symmetry S(a,b)+S(b,a)=ζ(a)ζ(b)+ζ(λ).

Methodological gap: §35 claims the odd-power rewriting 'removes all doubt' from the inductive law, but the page gives no proof. The rule is still exhibited on examples and then generalized. A rigorous proof of Euler's odd-weight formula came much later (Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn 1995).

ideas.what: Reduction of double (Euler) sums of odd weight m+n to ζ(λ) and products ζ(k)ζ(λ−k), with explicit binomial coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Euler's odd-weight reduction formula for double zeta values / linear Euler sums
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E477, 1775/76); rigorous proof Borwein, Borwein & Girgensohn 1995 ('Explicit evaluation of Euler sums')
ideas.where_published: E477 itself, Novi Commentarii Acad. Petrop. 20 (1776); Opera Omnia I.15

ideas.what: Using the symmetry ζ(2j)ζ(λ−2j) = ζ(λ−2j)ζ(2j) to rewrite the formula with only odd-indexed columns, making the coefficient law transparent
ideas.modern_name: Choice of a basis of weight-λ products of zeta values (odd-index normalization)

ideas.what: Coefficient of ζ(λ) equal to ½(1 ± C(λ,ν))
ideas.modern_name: ζ(λ)-coefficient in the BBG/Euler formula for ζ(s,t) with s+t odd

ideas.what: Binomial-coefficient notation n(ν) with n(ν)=0 for ν>n and n(ν)=n(n−ν)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Euler used similar notations elsewhere, e.g. [n/ν])

deep.surprise_reason: This is the core of Euler's well-known odd-weight double zeta formula from E477. It is widely cited in the multiple zeta literature (Borwein–Borwein–Girgensohn, Flajolet–Salvy, Zagier and others) and correctly credited to Euler. The table is correct and contains nothing beyond what is known.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'impares p^9 et p^7' — the image shows p^9 (slightly garbled 'p^9_d'), so p^2 ↔ p^9 and p^4 ↔ p^7 is correct.

Column header 'p^11' at left labels the coefficient ½(1±C(11,ν)) of ζ(11) in each row; the right-hand annotations '+p=p^{10}', '+p^3=p^8', etc. mean the extra product terms ζ(1)ζ(10), ζ(3)ζ(8), …, in which p^a and p^{λ−a} are paired.
